slot.brief: solve a homogeneous first-order DE by substituting y = vx, separating variables and integrating

stem: The general solution of the differential equation $(x^2 + y^2)\,dx = 2xy\,dy$ is

verdicts.working: Let z=y². Then z′=2y(dy/dx)=(x²+y²)/x=x+z/x, so (z/x)′=1. Hence y²=x²+Cx, or x²−y²=Cx.

working:
Rewrite as $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{x^2+y^2}{2xy} = \dfrac{1+(y/x)^2}{2(y/x)}$.  Let $y = vx$, $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = v + x\dfrac{dv}{dx}$.  Substitute: $v + x\dfrac{dv}{dx} = \dfrac{1+v^2}{2v}$.  Simplify: $x\dfrac{dv}{dx} = \dfrac{1-v^2}{2v}$.  Separate: $\dfrac{2v}{1-v^2}\,dv = \dfrac{dx}{x}$.  Integrate: $-\ln|1-v^2| = \ln|x| + C' \Rightarrow 1-v^2 = \dfrac{C}{x}$.  Substitute back $v = y/x$: $1 - \dfrac{y^2}{x^2} = \dfrac{C}{x} \Rightarrow x^2 - y^2 = Cx$.

Independent check: Let z=y². Then z′=2y(dy/dx)=(x²+y²)/x=x+z/x, so (z/x)′=1. Hence y²=x²+Cx, or x²−y²=Cx.
solution:
With $y=vx$, we have $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=v+x\dfrac{dv}{dx}$, so
$$x\dfrac{dv}{dx}=\dfrac{1-v^2}{2v},\qquad \dfrac{2v}{1-v^2}\,dv=\dfrac{dx}{x}.$$
Integrating gives $1-v^2=\dfrac{C}{x}$. Substituting $v=\dfrac{y}{x}$ yields $x^2-y^2=Cx$.
